nodes.title: The check-in's word 'safe' manufactures low-mood reads: after '…abhi safe hain?' a bare 'haan' read low mood 3/4, 'hmm' 4/4, 'haan theek hoon' 2/4 (each the full script on the next turn); after '…abhi theek hain?' all three 0/4 and 'pata nahi' 0/4, while 'nahi' (not okay) 4/4 and 'pata nahi, sab bekaar hai' 4/4 still read low (escalate, rightly). The old wording made the reply model ask 'safe / surakshit' in 7/16 check-in lines (often 'theek aur surakshit', two questions joined); the new 'okay, never safe' 0/16.

On a check-in, a WHOLE reply that is only 'I don't know' ('pata nahi', 'nahi pata', 'malum nahi', 'dont know', 'idk', 'not sure', 'kuch nahi', 'hmm', fine.js bareUnsure) is no answer yet, like a silence: the first waits (distressCheckAgain: it is okay not to know, she is right here, are you okay; no numbers, no incident) even over a model low-mood re-read, since the words read sees her question and the mood it reads is her last turn's; a second silence or 'pata nahi' in a row is the full script; a sure read of the same words escalates at once; a word more ('pata nahi, sab bekaar hai') is read as it stands. And the check-in asks if they are OKAY, never if they are safe (compile DISTRESS_CHECK, shapes distressCheck / distressCheckAgain). Refines dc-r144-checkin-next-turn, which released 'pata nahi' outright (the first cut's code escalated it instead: QA TEST 47f4bb3f U2b). Reverse if a sim-lab or QA disclosure answers the check-in with a bare 'pata nahi' and then goes quiet, or if the 'okay' wording misses a sure reply the 'safe' wording caught.

md.decisions:
## dc-r144-checkin-unsure — "pata nahi" waits once; the check-in asks "okay", never "safe" (2026-10-21)

QA's re-test of 08f86dc5 (TEST lesson 47f4bb3f, U2b): a low mood, the check-in "Kya aap abhi safe hain?", then "pata nahi" got the full script. Two causes. The words read sees her question, so its low-mood read of a bare "I don't know" is her last turn's mood; and the word "safe" (which the reply model chose in 7 of 16 check-ins, ms-r144-checkin-safe-word) turns even a "haan" into a low-mood read 3 times in 4. Now a bare "I don't know" waits once like a silence (it is okay not to know, she is here, are you okay), a second escalates, a sure read escalates at once; and the check-in asks if they are okay. With "okay" the same short replies read 0/4 while "nahi" (not okay) still reads low 4/4 and escalates.
md.measurements:
## ms-r144-checkin-safe-word (2026-10-21, n = 56 reads + 32 lines)

After "…abhi safe hain?": "haan" low 3/4, "hmm" 4/4, "haan theek hoon" 2/4, "nahi" sure 2/4 + low 2/4. After "…abhi theek hain?": those 0/4, 0/4, 0/4; "nahi" low 4/4; "pata nahi" 0/4 both; "pata nahi, sab bekaar hai" low 4/4 both. Check-in lines asking "safe / surakshit": old wording 7/16, new 0/16.
